meta.title: The Best Pizza Ovens
meta.description:
Here's my review of the very best outdoor standalone pizza ovens.

Get more details and results here: 
http://www.seriouseats.com/2017/05/best-backyard-pizza-ovens-review.html

transcript.text: making really great pizza requires a really really hot oven I'm talking about 900 degrees Fahrenheit or so if you want true in the apology style pizza now a home oven doesn't get that hot but fortunately there are a number of ovens on the market right now that allow you to achieve some of those temperatures outdoors for the last two months I have been making pizza almost every single day testing out about a dozen of these outdoor ovens to find which ones are the best here are my picks for the very best outdoor Pizza number for the pizzeria paronto at around $200 Distilled 11 is the oven of choice for budget weary cooks who are looking to get a slightly better than indoor oven performance in an outdoor space the high output ring-shaped burner is fueled by propane and heats up a double stack of pizza stones designed to diffuse heat and cook the bottom of your pizza evenly meanwhile the top of your piece of cooks does the hot air rising around the stones is deflected back downwards towards the pizza the air temperature the sub one can hit 6 to 700 degrees Fahrenheit with the floor temperature of around 550 degrees which means that it bakes pizzas up to 13 inches in size in around 5 minutes or so this is fast enough to get extra crispy results but you'll never achieve the poofy leopard spotted look of a pizza cooked in a hotter faster oven on the plus side because it's heated from underneath it's ready to cook your next pizza immediately after you've taken out the first one if you're looking for an easy to set up easy to operate and reliable oven for casual pizza nights and you favor extra crispy style pizzas over New York or Neapolitan styles the pizzeria pronto is a great choice number 3 the Blackstone this oven is the darling of Internet Pizza forums and with good reason it's a high-octane powerhouse switch it on and you'll hear a jet engine like roar as a gas flame shoots up the side of the unit it is a unique design which pairs of rotating base stones with a stationary ceiling all heated with a single large burner within 15 minutes the entire oven base dome and all welded temperatures in excess of 900 degrees Fahrenheit slide a pizza on to that stone which rotates with the help of an electric motor and watch as a spins around and cooks within 70 to 90 seconds you have a poofy leopard spotted beauty and because the oven heats from below it's immediately ready to fire the next pot so what are the downsides well there are a couple for one thing unless you've decorated your backyard to look like the cheap grill display in the parking lot of a Home Depot this oven will probably be the ugliest thing in it the other is build quality for $285 a tool this size may seem like a bargain but the corner cutting shows the plastic motor that came with mine failed after just a few uses though luckily any standard 3 inch rotisserie motor can be used to replace it adding a metal thrust bearing to the bottom of the rotating stand can also make it operate more smoothly by the 6th time I clicked in it the stone had cracked neatly in half and the heat proof paint on the inside started flaking off all of these problems can be fixed if you have a little mechanical know-how but it can be a headache for anyone who expects a product to work perfectly straight out of the box the rotating turntable also makes them mostly impractical for cooking anything but pizza still if you're fixing up a large volume of pizzas and shear performances what you're into the black stone is hard to beat once you've sprung for a few of the updates number 2 Lee Clooney Sooni was one of the first portable pizza ovens to come to market that could boast temperatures that rival full-blown wood-fired ovens if you're the kind of cook who really enjoys working with live fire including all of the joys and headaches that come with it the only three will reward you with truly wood-fired Neapolitan pizza to use it you light up a tray of wood pellets in the back of the unit then load up a metal hopper with more these pellets are pretty cheap you can get them for about 50 cents a pound at your local home goods store as the pellets burn gravity feeds more into the tray the flame gets pulled forward through the oven and up out a chimney mounted in the front within 15 to 20 minutes the dome temperature sits above 900 degrees Fahrenheit while the floor will hit around 750 degrees what is firing properly it can cook a crisp puffy Neapolitan pizza up to 12 inches wide in just 75 to 90 seconds but I say when it's firing properly because like all live fire cooking this oven is going to take some practice in working part wind patterns and weather can seriously affect how it burns there were times that I found the flame had gone completely out causing City black smoke to fill up the chamber and ruining more than one pizza in the process you really need to keep an eye on the fire and make adjustments as necessary opening up the pellet tray in the back or cracking the front door open to make sure that the flame is burning how it should be be prepared to put in some work because this oven definitely has a learning curve the all-metal construction is attractive and it looks great on the tabletop and the oven is large enough to cook other foods like steaks fish or vegetables it's also the most portable of the ovens I've tested coming in at just about 25 pounds with a carrying case which makes it a great little oven for picnics camping or the beach the base unit costs $300 and I think it's worth every penny the rumor has it that a gas conversion kit is coming for the Uni sometime in the summer of 2017 if this operates as promised that'll really be a game changer number one the Rock box this is my favorite out of all the ovens I tested it comes preassembled made out of heavy gauge stainless steel stone with a rubberized outer finish you can really feel how solidly machined and constructed this oven is like the Uni and the Presto it stands on the table top with metal legs and there are multiple options for fuel the standard burner box is a rocket stove style combustion chamber that allows you to feed hardwood or charcoal in through a tube on the side the flames are pulled up into the interior of the oven where they heat up the dome in the floor to temperatures in excess of 900 degrees Fahrenheit I fired this thing up using charcoal briquettes hard wood kindling and even scraps of cherry wood molding leftover from my kitchen cloth and it burns by you don't want to deal with live fire no problem the rocket stove swaps out for a gas burner that you could hook up to a standard propane tank which delivers a massive flame to the back of the oven in most cases I actually found that the gas flame heated it even better than wood the best part is so simple to use just switch it on and let it go no babysitting no monitoring and within half an hour it's ready to bake up a Neapolitan pizza with baked times of 75 to 90 seconds because the mouth of the oven doesn't need to be closed to operate like the Moonies does it's even easier to cook non pizza food flip the food into a cast-iron pan and slide it into the door of the oven with the handle hanging out for easy access the rock box also comes with an amazing aluminum pizza field it's perforated and textured to allow excess flour to fall away from your pizza instead of burning on the floor of the oven it's quickly become my favorite pizza peel because of its heavy insulation the sides of the rock box actually stay cool enough to touch with no danger of injury to you your kids or your pets even when it's in cold use the downsides well the mouth of the oven is only 12 inches wide which means that the largest pizzas even cooking it is about 11 inches forget about those large new york-style ties the only other downside is the price the southern is not cheap to order it and get it shipped to the United States cost a little over $600 making it double the cost of any of the other competitors up to that price you get a reliable easy to use powerhouse of an oven that will make you want to have a pizza party every single weekend [Music]
